# Tempest

Atari's 1981 arcade game: the same wells, enemies, rules and patterns, checked against the
arcade frame by frame as MAME emulates it.

The shape to notice:

- **The game is a dataset with its own rules.** `Game` (game.declare) holds what is in the
  well as records, and moves it on a frame at a time; the enemies' own rules are
  enemies.declare. The sixteen wells are well.declare; each wave's difficulty is a record in
  waves.json.
- **The arcade's chips are kept apart.** Random numbers come from the machine
  (machine.declare), which answers as the arcade's sound chips do.
- **The screen is views of the records.** The well, the claw, each enemy by its kind, the
  shots, explosions, spikes, nymphs and stars, the panel and the pages between games are each
  a view (screen.declare), drawn as lines of light (figures.declare) at the place and size the
  camera gives it (camera.declare: the perspective and the beam), in the colors and with the
  memory of the scene (scene.declare: what the screen remembers from frame to frame). The
  pictures, traced from the arcade's vector ROM, are pictures.json.
  The monitor works in the arcade's pixels and is scaled to the window.
- **The sounds are recordings.** sound.declare plays clips recorded from MAME's emulation of
  the arcade's two POKEY chips, as the game's records of each frame start them.

Keys: ← → or A S turn, Space or Return fire, ↓, Z or / superzapper, Return or 1 start, Escape pause,
C the panel that sets how the beam looks.

*This program is new code, written in Declare. It recreates the behavior of Tempest, Atari's
1981 arcade game, whose original program was written in 6502 assembly language (with Atari's
"Math Box" for its perspective), and reproduces its look and sound as closely as it can, frame
by frame. Tempest, its name, artwork, sounds and visual design belong to Atari, Inc. or its
successors; they are used here only to illustrate and test the Declare language, and no claim
is made to them. The MIT license of this repository covers this code, not the original game's
name, artwork or sounds. If you hold rights in this material and object to its being posted
here, please open an issue on this repository on GitHub, or message me there, and I will remove
it.*

include [ "machine.declare", "well.declare", "game.declare", "enemies.declare", "camera.declare", "scene.declare", "figures.declare", "beam.declare", "screen.declare", "sound.declare", "../touch-pad.declare" ]

defaultFlags [ render = canvas, accessibility = false ]

App [ appName = "Tempest", fill = black,
    wavesData: DataSource [ url = "waves.json", autoFetch = true, schema = [ waves[]: Wave ] ],
    picturesData: DataSource [ url = "pictures.json", autoFetch = true ],
    ready: boolean = { app.wavesData.loaded && app.picturesData.loaded },
    paused: boolean = false,

    machine: Machine [ ],
    well: Well [ ],
    game: Game [ machine = { app.machine }, well = { app.well }, waves = { app.wavesData.value?.waves ?? [] },
        pictureFrame(field: Playfield) { app.scene.advance(field) },
        pictureCleared() { app.scene.clear() }
        ] { {
        "claw": { "lane": 0, "position": 0, "depth": 0, "depthFraction": 0, "alive": true, "caught": false,
            "dropping": false, "fallSpeed": 0 },
        "enemies": [], "nymphs": [], "shots": [], "enemyShots": [], "blasts": [], "spikes": [], "spikeMarks": [], "stars": []
        } },

    camera: Camera [ game = { app.game }, well = { app.well }, pictures = { app.picturesData.value ?? {} } ],
    scene: Scene [ game = { app.game }, well = { app.well }, camera = { app.camera } ],
    screen: Monitor [ paused = { app.paused } ],
    speaker: SoundBoard [ game = { app.game }, paused = { app.paused } ],

    // how the beam looks, and the panel that sets it (beam.declare), shown and hidden by C

    beam: Beam [ ] { {
        "settings": [
            { "id": "glow", "label": "Bloom", "value": 0.85, "min": 0, "max": 1.5, "rich": 0.85, "plain": 0.5 },
            { "id": "spread", "label": "Bloom spread", "value": 1.6, "min": 0, "max": 4, "rich": 1.6, "plain": 1 },
            { "id": "halo", "label": "Halo", "value": 0.2, "min": 0, "max": 1, "rich": 0.2, "plain": 0 },
            { "id": "width", "label": "Beam width", "value": 1.25, "min": 0.4, "max": 3, "rich": 1.25, "plain": 1 },
            { "id": "core", "label": "White core", "value": 0.4, "min": 0, "max": 1, "rich": 0.4, "plain": 0.12 },
            { "id": "gain", "label": "Brightness", "value": 1, "min": 0.4, "max": 2, "rich": 1, "plain": 1 }
            ]
        } },
    tuning: boolean = false,
    beamPanel: BeamPanel [ x = { app.width - 276 }, y = 16, beam = { app.beam }, visible = { app.tuning } ],

    // The arcade's controls, on the keyboard. The spinner turns six steps a frame (a lane is
    // sixteen) while ← or → is held; Return also starts a game, as the coin and the start
    // button together.

    // A key pressed and let go between two of the game's frames still counts as pressed.

    // Escape pauses a game; any key goes on with it, and that key also counts as pressed, so a
    // turn or a shot held to go on carries on at once (as in Asteroids and Stargate).

    tapped: string[] = [],
    keys: Keys [
        onKeyDown(e: KeyEvent) {
            if (e.repeat || e.meta || e.ctrl || e.alt) return
            if (app.paused) { app.paused = false; if (e.key == "Escape") return }
            else if (e.key == "Escape") { if (app.game.playing) app.paused = true; return }
            if (e.code == "KeyC") { app.tuning = !app.tuning; return }
            app.tapped = [...app.tapped, e.code]
            }
        ],

    // the controls for one of the game's frames, taking the taps that frame has used; a
    // touch button (the pad, below) counts as its keys do

    takeControls() -> Controls {
        const tapped = app.tapped
        app.tapped = []
        const down = (button: string, ...keys: string[]) =>
            app.pad.isDown(button) || tapped.includes(button) || keys.some((k) => Keys.isDown(k) || tapped.includes(k))
        const pressed = (...keys: string[]) => keys.some((k) => tapped.includes(k))
        let turn = (down("right", "ArrowRight", "KeyS") ? 6 : 0) - (down("left", "ArrowLeft", "KeyA") ? 6 : 0)
        if (app.game.phase == "choosing") turn = this.chooseTurn(Math.sign(turn), pressed("ArrowRight", "KeyS", "ArrowLeft", "KeyA", "right", "left"))
        else wantChoice = -1
        return { turn, fire: down("fire", "Space", "Enter"), zap: down("zap", "ArrowDown", "KeyZ", "Slash"), start: down("start", "Enter", "Digit1") }
        },

    // On the "rate yourself" screen the keys step the choice a column at a time — once for a
    // press, and again every five frames while a key is held, after eight — where the arcade's
    // knob needs most of a turn for a column. The keys still only turn the spinner: as far as
    // it takes, a frame at a time, to bring the arcade's own choice to the column wanted.

    wantChoice: number = -1,
    heldFor: number = 0,

    chooseTurn(dir: number, fresh: boolean) -> number {
        const g = app.game
        if (wantChoice < 0) wantChoice = g.choice
        if (dir == 0) heldFor = 0
        else {
            heldFor = fresh ? 0 : heldFor + 1
            if (fresh || (heldFor >= 8 && (heldFor - 8) % 5 == 0))
                wantChoice = Math.max(0, Math.min(g.highestChoice, wantChoice + dir))
            }
        return wantChoice > g.choice ? 31 : wantChoice < g.choice ? -31 : 0
        },

    // The arcade's frame is nine or more ticks of its 246 Hz interrupt (the machine says how
    // many: about 36.6 ms, 27 a second, in play), not a whole number of a display's frames:
    // time banks between display frames, and the game moves on each time the last frame's
    // length has gathered.

    // The machine powers on at the first tick after the data has arrived, not when the App is
    // built, so a test replaying a recording can set the machine up first (which stops the
    // clock), power it on itself (setting `started`) and step every frame.

    started: boolean = false,
    clock: Time [ tick = frame, running = { app.ready && !app.paused && !app.machine.replaying },
        banked: number = 0,
        onTick(dt: number) {
            if (!app.started) { app.game.powerOn(); app.started = true }
            banked = Math.min(banked + dt, 0.15)       // after a stall, catch up at most about four frames
            while (banked >= app.machine.frameTicks * app.machine.tick) {
                banked = banked - app.machine.frameTicks * app.machine.tick
                app.game.step(app.takeControls())
                }
            }
        ],

    // On a touch screen, the arcade's controls as its panel has them: the spinner, as two
    // buttons that turn it, under the left hand; superzapper and fire under the right
    // (../touch-pad.declare). A press shorter than a frame still counts, as a key's does.
    // Over the screen, start sits low on the left, clear of the credits across its foot.

    pad: TouchPad [ startShown = { !app.game.playing }, ink = yellow, startOverLeft = true,
        fieldX = { app.screen.x }, fieldY = { app.screen.y },
        fieldW = { app.screen.width * app.screen.zoom }, fieldH = { app.screen.height * app.screen.zoom },
        buttonDown(id: string) { app.tapped = [...app.tapped, id] },
        keys = { [
            { id: "left", label: "SPIN LEFT", icon: "ccw", side: "left", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "right", label: "SPIN RIGHT", icon: "cw", side: "left", col: 1, row: 0 },
            { id: "zap", label: "SUPER ZAPPER", side: "right", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "fire", label: "FIRE", side: "right", col: 1, row: 0 }
            ] }
        ]
    ]
